definitions.explanation: Vibrations that travel through air or other media and can be heard. Includes all kinds of sounds, from music to everyday noises.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きい{音|おと}を{聞|き}きました。
{音|おと}を{小|ちい}さくしてください。
{外|そと}で{大|おお}きい{音|おと}がしましたが、{何|なに}か{分|わ}かりませんでした。
examples.english: There was a loud sound outside, but I couldn't tell what it was.

examples.japanese: {夜|よる}{静|しず}かな{時|とき}に{小|ちい}さい{音|おと}が{聞|き}こえると、ちょっと{怖|こわ}いです。{何|なに}の{音|おと}か{分|わ}からないからです。
examples.english: When I hear small sounds at night when it's quiet, it's a bit scary. It's because I don't know what the sound is.

notes:
{音|おと} refers to sounds in general, especially non-vocal sounds. Different from {声|こえ} (voice), which specifically refers to sounds made by humans or animals.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {音|おと}がする (a sound is heard/made)
- {音|おと}を{立|た}てる (to make a sound)
- {音|おと}が{聞|き}こえる (to be able to hear a sound)
- {音|おと}を{小|ちい}さくする (to turn down the volume)

COMPOUND WORDS:
- {足音|あしおと} (footsteps)
- {物音|ものおと} (sound of something)
- {音楽|おんがく} (music)
- {音声|おんせい} (audio, voice)
- {騒音|そうおん} (noise, din)
- {雑音|ざつおん} (static, noise)

READINGS:
Usually おと, but often おん in compounds: {音量|おんりょう} (volume), {発音|はつおん} (pronunciation).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {声|こえ}: voice (human/animal sounds)
- {響|ひび}き: resonance, echo
